question: When static-v2 board values are held fixed, does enabling the profile-derived promotion bonus improve finite-budget outcomes over the same static-board/Unit-hand candidate with the bonus disabled?
changed_premise: The completed promotion-bonus panel used Unit board/hand values and did not test how the existing bonus interacts with the retained scoped static-board candidate. The integrated package changed board, hand, bonus and ordering together and could not attribute this component. A fresh bonus-only contrast at fixed static board values can decide whether this component belongs in the scoped static candidate.

roots.selection: Retain every deterministic legal-random generated root; no outcome, exposure, action or price filtering; no replacement.

arms.fixed_foe: The bonus-off evaluator with the same static board values and Unit hand values used by the candidate; this fixed foe is identical in both arms.
arms.candidate_only_change: Both candidate arms use the same static-v2 board profile, Unit hand values, static-derived promotion_gain_by_type, default capture/type ordering and dynamic terms. Only promotion_potential_weight changes from 0 to 3. The bonus-off candidate is also the fixed foe.
arms.search: Existing public Python AlphaBeta, StagedMovePicker disabled, transposition table off, root tactical fallback disabled identically.

analysis.primary: Pair bonus-on minus bonus-off rewards by exact root and candidate owner; each UNKNOWN endpoint contributes its legal [-1,+1] reward range before differencing.
analysis.robustness: Report all slots, owner, odd/even root parity, and leave-one-seed-out finite bounds.
analysis.cost: Report candidate nodes and caller seconds separately; no standalone wall-time utility claim.
analysis.retain_rule: Retain this component for the scoped static-board candidate only if reward lower bounds are strictly positive overall, both owners, both parities and every leave-one-seed-out view, or median candidate-node reduction is at least 10% overall and in both owner/parity strata while no corresponding utility lower bound is negative. Otherwise exclude the bonus from the scoped candidate; do not change the global evaluator default.

integrity: Use fresh generated rules and roots with full history; preserve promotion, drops, auxiliary state and adjudication.
Keep all UNKNOWN, actual terminal, failure and unstarted slots; no top-up, refit or default change.
Verify static board, Unit hand, capture_order_value and type_value are equal across candidate arms; only promotion potential changes.
Bound the run at 3600 seconds and stop if work exceeds frozen resource caps.

cost.threshold: Expected and capped runtime below 120 minutes.
cost.basis: Adjacent matched 64-game generated 5x5 D3 panels completed in 222.656–246.656 seconds; this adds no training or solver work.

decision_after: A passing finite retention gate would justify only the bonus component within the 5x5-scoped static candidate. Failure closes this context-specific bonus route. Neither outcome is a general promotion-price law or global default authorization.
